title: Asynchronous JS
description: Handling asynchronous code with Promises and async/await.

lessons.title: What is Asynchronous JavaScript?
lessons.content: Asynchronous JavaScript allows your program to perform tasks without blocking the main thread, enabling smoother user experiences by handling operations like data fetching or timers in the background.

lessons.title: Callbacks
Problems with Callbacks
lessons.content: Callbacks can lead to nested, hard-to-read code known as 'callback hell,' making error handling and flow control complex.

lessons.title: Promises Introduction
lessons.content: Promises are objects representing the eventual completion or failure of an asynchronous operation, providing cleaner syntax and better error handling than callbacks.

lessons.title: Creating and Using Promises
Promise Chaining
Async/Await Syntax
Error Handling with Async/Await
Promise.all and Promise.race
lessons.content: Promise.all waits for multiple promises to resolve, while Promise.race resolves or rejects as soon as one promise settles, useful for concurrent async operations.

lessons.title: Practical Use Cases
lessons.content: Asynchronous JavaScript is crucial in web development for tasks such as API calls, reading files, or handling timers, allowing responsive applications.
